reasons: Both answers correct the premise at the start ('800 is certainly illegal', the company does not decide alone). Both explain that 83号 expired on 2026-08-15, give the 2192 floor with 1392 short, and give 6400 as a contract or handbook figure at 80%, not 70%. B goes further on the base: it lists the excluded items (bonuses, meal, transport and housing allowances, overtime), though it gives no 21.75 daily formula. Its HR message also follows the key more closely: it asks for the gross, deductions and net breakdown, asks HR to cite the specific clause, and sets a reply deadline, and B names 12333 among the remedies. A says nothing about base composition and adds a confusing 4480 row with no sound legal basis. A's HR message does not ask whether 800 is the gross or the net amount. B's main slip is the oversimplified 'one-year time limit' for arbitration. That is smaller than A's gaps, so B wins clearly.
